current_definition: Present from birth; belonging to a person's character or ability from the very beginning, not learned through experience.
Belonging to something as its essential, fundamental character; valuable or true in and of itself, not because of external factors.
Given to examining one's own thoughts, feelings, and motivations; turned inward rather than toward the outside world.
Relating to ordinary, everyday life; lacking excitement or special interest; routine and unremarkable.
So strong or obvious that it can almost be physically felt; capable of being touched or clearly perceived by the senses.
Clearly and obviously true; plain to see without any need for explanation or argument.
To read or look over something carefully and with close attention, taking time to absorb the details.
To think deeply and at length about something, turning it over repeatedly in the mind.
To examine something very closely and critically, looking for flaws, details, or hidden information.
Real and concrete enough to be touched or clearly experienced; not abstract or imaginary.
Complete and total, with no exceptions or limitations; not relative to anything else.
Existing as a concept or idea rather than as a concrete, physical thing; dealing with general principles rather than specific examples.
Having no clear or fixed shape, structure, or definition; vague and without definite boundaries.
Something — a person, object, idea, or custom — that belongs to a different time period and seems out of place in the present.
Absolute and unconditional; stated without any exceptions, doubts, or qualifications.
(lowercase) Including or concerning a very wide range of things; broad in scope and interests; universal in reach.
An impossible or wildly unrealistic idea or hope; something that exists only in the imagination and cannot be achieved.
Final, authoritative, and settling a question completely; the most reliable or complete version of something.
Relating to a method of reaching truth or understanding by weighing opposing arguments against each other; involving debate between contradictory positions.
Unchanging and unchangeable; remaining the same forever regardless of circumstances.
To place two things side by side in order to highlight the contrast or relationship between them.
A statement or situation that seems contradictory or impossible but may in fact reveal a deeper truth.
Speech or writing that speaks about God or sacred things in a deeply disrespectful or offensive way.
To call upon a spirit or supernatural power through a ritual or spoken words.
Relating to ancient occult or mystical traditions, especially those involving alchemy or secret knowledge.
A belief or opinion that goes against the official teachings of a religion or other established system of thought, and is therefore considered dangerous or wrong by those in authority.
A set of words spoken aloud as part of a magic ritual or religious ceremony, believed to have a special power when recited.
Impossible to take back, change, or undo; final and permanent.
Not sacred or holy; belonging to the ordinary, worldly realm rather than the spiritual one. Can also describe language or behavior that shows disrespect for sacred things.
To openly declare or claim a belief, feeling, or quality, especially one relating to faith.
To try to persuade others to convert to one's own religion, belief, or cause, often in a persistent or aggressive way.
A physical act of treating something sacred—a holy object, place, or person—with extreme disrespect or contempt.
So holy or important that it must never be questioned, criticized, or changed; treated as completely beyond challenge.
The study of the nature of God, religious belief, and the relationship between humanity and the divine, typically as an academic or formal discipline.
(noun) A person who believes that whether a god exists is unknown and perhaps unknowable, taking neither a believing nor a disbelieving position.
A person who does not believe in the existence of God or any gods.
To interpret or understand the meaning of something in a particular way, especially a statement, action, or law.
To spread information, ideas, or beliefs widely among a large number of people.
Narrowly focused on one's own community or way of life, and unwilling or unable to consider outside perspectives or experiences.
A lack of foresight or the failure to consider the long-term consequences of one's actions; short-sightedness in thinking or planning.
Having a very limited or narrow outlook, concerned only with local matters and uninterested in broader ideas or the wider world.
(adjective) Characteristic of or limited to a province or region, especially in having an unsophisticated or narrow view of the world beyond one's own locality.
Not connected to or controlled by religious institutions, beliefs, or authority; belonging to the ordinary, non-sacred world.
A harsh, jarring mixture of loud sounds that are unpleasant or difficult to bear.
The rhythmic rise and fall of a voice, piece of writing, or piece of music, giving it a pleasing and flowing quality.
Tending to talk at great length about trivial or unimportant matters, often to the point of becoming tedious or annoying to listeners.
To use energetic or dramatic hand and arm movements while speaking, usually to emphasise or express what one is saying.
Excessively dramatic or theatrical in behaviour or speech; designed to attract attention through overblown emotional display rather than genuine feeling.
A deliberate and obvious exaggeration used for emphasis or dramatic effect, not meant to be taken literally.
Tending to talk a great deal; very chatty or talkative, sometimes engagingly so.
